rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.5 and 3.1-3.4 report the authors' own case study in a 3.3 ha Verdicchio plot in the Marche Region: three airborne thermal surveys with CWSI maps (Table 1, Figure 6), Bioristor in vivo sensors with Sentek multilevel soil water probes monitored for ~150 days (Figures 9-10), platform water balance runs, and a questionnaire-based cost analysis (Tables 2-4).
rows.notes: The study does not report any own result showing that soil sensors deliver water use efficiency or water savings. The pilot vineyard has no irrigation system (Section 2.1; Conclusions state this as a limitation), so no sensor-guided irrigation was performed. Soil water probes were used only to monitor soil water content and to compare with the Bioristor signal (Section 3.3, Figure 10); the thermal/CWSI maps and Bioristor detected water stress periods and spatial variability. The WP/EWP indices (Table 4) compare a non-irrigated 2020 season with an estimated 2021 irrigated scenario (yield and costs marked as estimated), and WP actually decreased under the hypothetical irrigation; this is not evidence that sensors improved water use efficiency. The study supports only the precondition (monitoring/detection of water stress), not the claimed optimization or efficiency effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.5 and 3.1-3.4 report the authors' own case study (thermal surveys, Bioristor and soil probe monitoring, platform water balance runs, cost questionnaire; Tables 1-4, Figures 6-10).
rows.notes: No own result links soil sensors to maintained or improved grape yield or quality. The vineyard was not irrigated, so no sensor-based irrigation outcome on yield was measured. Table 3 gives a real 2021 yield of 86 q/ha (drought-reduced) and an 'estimated' 103 q/ha had the winery irrigated in response to sensor-detected stress; this is an assumption, not a measured effect, and quality was not measured. The Bioristor section notes that water shortage affected flowering and veraison and suggests mild irrigation 'could have been scheduled', which is a recommendation. The study therefore only supports the upstream step (detecting water stress), not the yield/quality effect.

notes: Full text appears complete (some OCR duplication of figure captions). Study is a single-plot prototype/case study in central Italy; the main sensing results concern airborne thermal CWSI maps and the Bioristor in vivo sensor, with Sentek soil probes used only as comparison data. No irrigation was applied in the study plot; economic indices for irrigation are simulated using neighbouring-plot costs and an estimated yield.
